title: Sprinklr’s Revenue Grew Just 1% and the Stock Fell 9%. Can AI Innovation Break the Slump?

content_html:
Sprinklr shares fell 8.55% on September 2 after the company reported fiscal second-quarter 2027 results. Total revenue increased only 1% to $213.7 million, while subscription revenue rose 3% to $194.8 million. For a software company marketing AI-powered customer experience tools, that pace makes the central issue unavoidable: Sprinklr, Inc. (NYSE:CXM) must show that product innovation can restart growth rather than merely protect an installed base.

Rawpixel.com/Shutterstock.com

There are constructive signals beneath the weak headline. Remaining performance obligations reached $1.03 billion, up 11%, which provides contracted revenue visibility. Sprinklr serves more than 1,600 enterprises, including 59% of the Fortune 100. Its platform brings customer-service, social-media, marketing, and analytics data together, giving its AI tools context that a standalone assistant may lack. Free cash flow of $13.1 million also shows the company is not relying entirely on external financing.

The income statement explains the selloff. GAAP operating income fell to $10 million from $16.3 million a year earlier, and non-GAAP operating income declined to $31.3 million from $38.2 million. Management guided full-year revenue to $866.5 million to $868.5 million, a range that does not imply a rapid return to growth. Large customers can consolidate vendors, delay projects, or test lower-cost AI alternatives before expanding contracts.

Professional investors reduced their collective exposure before the report. Insider Monkey counted 28 hedge funds holding Sprinklr, Inc. (NYSE:CXM) at the end of Q2, down from 34 in Q1. Solel Partners reported 3,649,369 shares as of June 30 and remained the largest listed hedge-fund holder. A concentrated owner can press for value creation, although the filing says nothing about an acquisition or the timing of an operating turn.

Reported short interest declined before the earnings drop. The August 14 settlement showed 9.13 million shares short, or 5.21% of float, down 31.2% from 13.27 million on July 31, with 3.4 days to cover. The data show fewer open short positions, not why individual traders changed them.

Sprinklr has assets that matter: large customers, a billion-dollar contracted backlog, and data-rich workflows. The missing piece is acceleration. AI becomes an investment catalyst only when it lifts renewals, expansion, and revenue growth. Until those measures improve, the stock can remain cheap for reasons that are operational rather than merely emotional. The next earnings report should be judged on subscription growth and RPO conversion before adjusted earnings. Cost control can protect profit for a while, but a software platform ultimately needs customers to expand spending. That is the evidence the current valuation still lacks.
